newsitem.title: UK: UK Nat Power brings back oil power plant for winteR.
newsitem.headline: UK Nat Power brings back oil power plant for winteR.

text.p: Britain's National Power Plc has brought back on stream a mothballed oil-burning power station in Pembroke, Wales to replace a damaged coal-fired plant in Aberthaw, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
The 500 megawatt (mW) unit, one of four at the Pembroke site, was brought back on stream last week at the request of the National Grid after problems were encountered at the 500 mW Aberthaw plant.
Pembroke power station was mothballed in March this year ahead of its planned conversion to burn Orimulsion, a Venezuelan bitumen fuel.
"The Pembroke unit will be available to help meet winter peak demand, but how much oil it runs is impossible to predict," a spokesman said.
Last winter, Britain's electricity grid was pushed very near to full capacity by unusually strong demand.
